reasons: Rule correctly triggered: § 2.1 is a three-year, USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right, which is the MINCOMMIT walk-away position, so a 'deviation' status with an actionable redline is appropriate.

Redline is directionally correct and customer-favourable: it removes the minimum/take-or-pay obligation and limits payment to Services ordered under an Order Form (preferred position), without adding unrelated obligations or new Vendor rights.

The failed minimal-edit check (0.943 changed characters) is acceptable here because the entire paragraph is the offending commitment; the operative effect is a deletion plus a short confirming statement, which is the least-invasive way to implement 'delete or narrow' guidance.

Comment complies with tone and format: concise, first person plural, '[Playbook]' prefix, states what changed and why, cross-references the consistent § 12.3 acknowledgement, and offers the 12-month reducible commitment with true-up as the fallback.
No internal inconsistency created — the edit aligns § 2.1 with § 12.3 (no minimum-volume commitment) and § 7.1 (fees limited to Order Form amounts).
